<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I am designing the Reporter interface.

The Reporter interface defines three formats: human, json, and agents. It exposes two methods, `reportAnalyze` and `reportFix`, each accepting typed options objects for verbose output, graph inclusion, dry-run mode, content inclusion, and error payloads.

The design now treats stdout as the adapter itself. Human, JSON, and agents are three separate adapters. Current handlers mix orchestration with presentation logic. I will extract human formatters into their own module, create the Reporter interface, and let cli-program wire the selected adapter.

Dedicated test fixtures will be created for the acceptance criteria. A unified `--format` flag will select the reporter, with `--json` kept as a backward-compatible alias. The agents subcommand will continue using its dedicated reporter directly.

I will place the Reporter interface and factory in `src/reporter.ts`. Human formatters will move to `src/reporter-human.ts`. I am weighing whether to split JSON and agents into separate files or keep them consolidated.

JSON and agents adapters will be thin wrappers around existing cli-json and cli-output modules. Handlers will receive a reporter instance and delegate all output to it. The cli-program action will resolve the format option and pass the correct reporter into the analysis runner. Agents format carries distinct semantics, including an envelope schema version and a separate `--include-graph` flag.

Handlers will accept a Reporter instance and delegate all output to it. They will stop branching on the `--json` flag. `runAnalyzeCommand` will validate inputs, resolve files, run analysis, and then call `reporter.reportAnalyze` with typed options. Error paths will route through the reporter too.

Exit code logic stays in handlers rather than the reporter. Reporters will only handle presentation. Agents error envelopes remain in cli-agents or pass through AgentsReporter. The design introduces a `CliFormat` type.

The Reporter interface now includes a `readonly format` property. Its `analyze` and `fix` methods accept typed input objects carrying results, errors, verbose flags, graph inclusion, and command metadata. An `emptyStdout()` method handles early-exit cases such as missing configuration or zero matched files.

Early-exit outputs differ by format. Human writes nothing to stdout. JSON writes `[]`. Agents writes a full envelope. A single `emptyStdout` method is insufficient. Reporters should instead expose targeted failure methods such as `reportConfigError` or `reportNoFiles`. The `reportAnalyzeSuccess` method may return a suggested exit code.

The interface is simplified to `analyze` and `fix` methods plus an `emitFailurePlaceholder` for early failures. Machine formats emit a placeholder on failure while human does nothing. Agents still needs special casing because its envelope must carry errors.

I will keep the agents subcommand intact and refactor it to delegate emission to AgentsReporter while preserving its orchestration logic. Golden tests will cover the three formats against the specified fixture files.

Snapshot tests will disable ANSI colors by setting NO_COLOR=1, since picocolors respects that environment variable. Ready to begin implementation.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Beginning implementation of the full solution.

Mapping out the reporter architecture. A new `src/reporter.ts` module will define the format interface and factory. A separate `src/reporter-human.ts` will hold all human formatting logic. `cli-handlers.ts`, `cli-agents.ts`, `cli-options.ts`, and `cli-program.ts` will be updated to wire the new Reporter seam. Fixtures and golden tests will follow.

The `Reporter` interface defines `reportAnalyze` and `reportFix` methods. Each accepts typed options objects for analyze and fix operations. The interface also includes a `format` property and a placeholder for stdout when commands fail before returning results.

Adding `reportEarlyFailure` to the `Reporter` interface for pre-results command failures. The `createReporter` factory switches on `CliFormat` to instantiate the correct adapter. A `resolveFormat` helper will derive the active format from CLI options.

`resolveFormat` prioritizes an explicit `--format` flag, then falls back to `--json`, then defaults to `"human"`.

`reportEarlyFailure` is format-specific. Human mode writes nothing to stdout because stderr already carries the error. JSON mode prints `"[]"`. Agents mode emits an envelope containing the errors.

Handlers will accept a `Reporter` instance directly. The analyze flow checks for a build error before invoking the reporter.

The analyze handler will call `emitCliError` for build failures, then invoke `reporter.reportEarlyFailure` before exiting. Normal results pass through `reportAnalyze` with verbose and graph flags. Command names for the reporter options are being aligned with existing envelope conventions.

The agents reporter will use the command name "agents/analyze" for both the dedicated agents subcommand and the --format agents option on analyze. This keeps the envelope schema consistent across both entry points.

Existing handler names like `runHumanAnalyze` will stay unchanged to minimize churn in `cli-program`. They will gain a `reporter` parameter with a default that creates a reporter from resolved CLI options. This lets tests pass a mock reporter while the program passes the real one. Fix handlers will also need agent-format conversion helpers.
</details></think>
